notes: The physical mesh is row-major with 9 rows and 6 columns.
The analytical network lists dimensions as columns then rows.

The die node (die rollout stage 1, 2026-10-03) replaces compute.peak-perf-tflops: peak compute, local-mem bandwidth and capacity are derived by the shared die cost library (mutually exclusive with a compute node); the die point matches the base hardware (0.75 MiB / user grid required / 800 mm2 / 512 bit / legacy HBM 4x1 at 1640 GB/s).
D2D latency is modeled as a per-hop adjacent-link latency.
The remote-memory pool is attached to every physical mesh-boundary NPU.
The 512 GB/s remote-memory bandwidth and 100 ns latency are shared simulator assumptions.
The capacity profile describes local HBM placement per NPU.
D2D bandwidth twin of face_case5_config_c.json (WP7 hardware twin set): only d2d.bandwidth-gbps differs from the base source (4050.0 -> 8100.0 GB/s, x2); every other field is identical.

Derived rho = B_D2D/B_HBM = 8100.0/1640.0 ~= 4.9390 (simplified analytical anchor, design doc section 1.2); the anchor's parity band d <= rho widens versus the base configuration's 4050/1640 ~= 2.4695.

Twin set: _d2d_x05 (2025 GB/s) / _d2d_x2 (8100 GB/s) / _d2d_sub (1200 GB/s). The _d2d_sub tier is a rho < 1 configuration: the anchor's bandwidth-parity condition fails even for a single flow; this does not preclude system-level gains from lower remote compute load or smaller target capacity pressure, the benefit direction is not preset, and the selection-rate-profile domain shape is an open research question (C20 item 5).

User-authorized engineering comparison point (2026-10-16): 10 x 10 Core grid on a 25 mm x 32 mm compute Die (800 mm2), 0.75 MiB SRAM/Core and 512-bit NoC. Architectural PE peak is 126.6 INT4 TOPS, numerically compared with the TX8 128 BF16 TFLOPS reference; precision and independent measurement are not equivalent. Vec FP32-equivalent peak is 12.65728 T eq-op/s, not the TX8 1 T reference. Legacy HBM remains the preserved 4 x 16 GB / 410 GB/s per-stack reference (64 GB and 1640 GB/s), not current DOCX HBM3E.

Factory compute default (phase 2, 2026-10-18): the coarse-die node (coarse_die_v2 typed descriptor, materialized verbatim into resolved_die_model.json) replaces the legacy die node as the checked-in backend; die (mesh_die_v1) and compute.peak-perf-tflops remain supported as mutually exclusive alternatives and their aligned capacity profiles are kept for explicit fixtures.

2026-10-21 wafer-fit default redesign (user-directed): the checked-in coarse-die architecture block is now the maximum compute Die that still fits the 9x6 die mesh inside the 215x215 mm system region under the legacy 10% interconnect reserve (effective extent = outline/sqrt(0.9)): die 33.99448 x 22.66298 mm = 770.416 mm2 (215*sqrt(0.9)/6 by 215*sqrt(0.9)/9, five-decimal truncation inward), 13x9 Core grid (117 Cores), 1.5 MiB SRAM/Core, 256-bit NoC; architectural peaks 833.04 INT4 TOPS and 83.300724 Vec FP32-eq TFLOPS per die (best >=256-bit row of the 32-row table at this outline). The prior 25x32 mm / 10x10 / 0.75 MiB / 512-bit block could not host the 9-row direction of the mesh (9x32=288>215 even at zero reserve; only 6 rows at the 10% reserve) and remains verbatim in die/configs/tx8_compute_matched_hardware.json, which keeps its 2026-10-16 authorization and numbers. HBM stays 2 rows x 2 stacks x 36 GB = 144 GB per die at 4710.4 GB/s (validation-coarse-144g unchanged); the bump budget at 770.416 mm2 (~31,835 GB/s) still covers HBM plus the 4050 GB/s D2D links. The wafer array counts the compute Die outline; the two-row co-planar HBM module outline (34.29 x 45.22 mm) is a packaging-layer diagnostic and does not gate the wafer mesh.
